clue.text: It doesn't matter if just one of the pair hesitates

definitions.meaning: a dismissive phrase telling someone the effort is not needed

definitions.text: if just one of the pair hesitates
definitions.meaning: read as 'do not both say er': two people should not both hesitate, so only one of the pair does

explanation.surface: A remark about two people where only one of them falters, and it is of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into DON'T BOTH ER, an instruction that the two of a pair not both utter the hesitation sound 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom brushing off a task as not worth the trouble, the same as saying nothing hangs on it.

clue.text: Foreigner who loses it when she gets married

definitions.text: Foreigner who loses it when she gets married

parts.words: Foreigner who loses it when she gets married
parts.note: a young unmarried Spanish woman whose title, on marriage, drops its final two letters, the syllable spelling 'it', to become the title for a wife

explanation.surface: An outsider who somehow loses something on her wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses it' sounds like losing her composure, but the woman literally loses the letters I and T: the Spanish title for a miss becomes señora, the title for a married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish courtesy title for a young unmarried lady is used in English for any Spanish girl, a foreigner here.

clue.text: A din that's audible is irritating

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the phrase is replaced by a word sounding the same when spoken

parts.note: a din is a noise, so 'a din' gives A NOISE

explanation.surface: A loud racket that can be heard is getting on someone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate them; the verb is in the same third-person form as the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Touched, dead astern

parts.note: D is a standard abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and in genealogies
astern means at the back of a ship, which sailors call aft

explanation.surface: A sailor's report that something is affected and lifeless at the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touched' looks like a verb about contact, but it is the informal adjective meaning slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched is an informal word for mildly crazy, the same sense as silly or foolish.

clue.text: Theatres where they now indulge in games of bingo

parts.note: to indulge in a game is to play it
in bingo the winning call is 'house!', and the game itself has long been called house or housey-housey

explanation.surface: Old theatres now turned into bingo halls.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British cinemas and theatres were converted to bingo halls, which is the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a theatre, a building where plays are staged.

clue.text: You can't miss this store opening

parts.note: a barn is a farm building used for storing hay and grain
a door is an opening into a building

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a shop opening that nobody should miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store opening' reads as a shop's launch, but it is the doorway of a storage building. A shot that misses a barn door is proverbially hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is the stock example of a target too big to miss, as in 'couldn't hit a barn door'.

clue.text: The Greeks had a word for it, I've discovered

definitions.text: The Greeks had a word for it
definitions.meaning: a Greek exclamation, famously Archimedes' in his bath
the literal meaning of the Greek word, I have found it

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly reports finding something the ancient Greeks already named.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of triumph at a discovery is Greek for 'I have found it', so it is both Greek and a declaration of finding.

clue.text: Grounds or pastures, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to take a word that sounds like this one

parts.note: leas are meadows or pastures, a poetic word

explanation.surface: A question of whether some land is lawns or meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like land, next to pastures, but it means the sediment at the bottom of a drink, like coffee grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs or sediment that settle out of wine, just as grounds settle out of coffee.

clue.text: Unexceptional combination of extremes

definitions.meaning: read literally as without exception, everybody included
one is the smallest whole number and all is everything, so joining them unites the two extremes

explanation.surface: Something ordinary that brings opposites together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexceptional' usually means ordinary; here it means with no exceptions at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means every single person, so it admits no exceptions.

clue.text: Serious but not grave

definitions.meaning: an ... illness or crisis is a severe one
in accents, the ... slopes the opposite way to the grave

explanation.surface: Describing a situation as worrying but not yet critical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' reads as a synonym of serious, but it is the name of an accent mark, which the acute accent is not.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute problem is a severe and urgent one, the sense of serious in 'a serious shortage'.

clue.text: Dated and removed

definitions.meaning: to have dated someone is to have escorted them out socially
taken away or extracted, as a tooth

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned that has been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' wants to be the adjective meaning old-fashioned; it is the past tense of going on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to go on a date with them, and to take something out is to remove it.

clue.text: Statesmen making bets

definitions.meaning: read as men of the States, Americans
a Yankee is a British bookmaker's term for a combination wager of eleven bets on four horses

explanation.surface: Politicians who gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesmen' reads as politicians but means men from the United States. In British betting shops a Yankee is a multiple bet covering four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans are informally called by the nickname for northerners, and bets of that combined type share the name.

clue.text: Newspaper's deadlines cut

parts.note: the death notices in a paper, lines about the dead, with their full name shortened

explanation.surface: A newspaper has had its time limits for copy reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadlines' looks like press cut-offs, but it is dead lines, notices about people who have died, and 'cut' says the word is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Obituaries are a newspaper's notices of deaths, and the word is commonly clipped in journalism.

clue.text: Snack bar?

parts.note: not a café but a bar you eat as a snack, a slab of a cocoa confection

explanation.surface: A place to buy a quick bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'snack bar' is not a café but a bar that is itself a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of the cocoa sweet is a common snack, so it is literally a snack in bar form.

clue.text: Severely judge a friend

parts.note: a critic judges books, plays or performances
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: An instruction to be harsh in assessing one's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a verb applied to a friend; it is the noun, someone who judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Critically ill means severely ill, so the adverb carries the sense of seriously or gravely.

clue.text: Sort of school where merely neat composition is required

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the words are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A school where pupils' written work need only be tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' looks like a school essay, which suits the surface, but it signals rearranging MERELY NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An elementary school is a primary school, a kind of school for young children, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Is it of any benefit to us? Well, no!

definitions.text: Is it of any benefit to us? Well, no!

parts.words: Is it of any benefit to us? Well, no!
parts.note: a policy that pays out benefit only when the policyholder is not well, ie falls ill

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts whether something is worthwhile and decides it isn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, no!' reads as a grudging denial, but it means 'when not well': the cover pays out only if we are ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover against illness pays benefits for medical costs only when the insured person is sick.

clue.text: Revealing story of Swiss resistance?

indicators.note: a story of someone puts the hero's name first, as a possessive label before the word for the narrative

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary hero of Swiss resistance against Austrian rule
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A revealing account of how the Swiss resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell, who shot an apple off his son's head, is a Swiss folk hero of resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is one that reveals or betrays something hidden.

clue.text: When the water moving ain't deep

definitions.text: When the water moving ain't deep

indicators.note: moving means changing position, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of the sea when it is shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges AIN'T DEEP; the whole clue also describes the occasion when the sea's rise and fall is least.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide occurs twice a month and has the smallest range, so the high water is least deep.

clue.text: I'm held back by exchanges of shots in battle

indicators.note: held means gripped within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: in tennis a rally is an exchange of shots

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the letters of I'm are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone pinned down by gunfire during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchanges of shots' suggests gunfire but means tennis rallies. Ramillies was a 1706 battle where Marlborough beat the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramillies, in present-day Belgium, is the site of a famous battle in the War of the Spanish Succession.

clue.text: Crocodile, one that attacks human beings

definitions.meaning: a broad-snouted crocodile of India
a street robber who assaults people

explanation.surface: A man-eating crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single man-eater; the two halves are a species of crocodile and a street robber.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh crocodile of the Indian subcontinent is named from Hindi, and the street robber who assaults victims shares the word.

clue.text: "Stretch" or "bird"

definitions.meaning: to strain the neck forward to see better
a tall wading bird with a long neck

explanation.surface: Two words offered as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: One stretches the neck to see over a crowd, and the long-necked wading bird has the same name.

clue.text: He plays Shakespearean part for the network

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
a spider's web of fine threads

explanation.surface: An actor takes a Shakespeare role for a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Network' suggests a broadcaster who hired an actor; it is the spider's silky mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a network of fine threads, and one of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears that name.

clue.text: A target set for crafty rivals

definitions.text: A target set for crafty rivals

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A goal laid down for cunning competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests cunning but means in boats, rivals in craft; 'set' rearranges A TARGET, and the whole clue describes the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a contest between rivals in craft.

clue.text: Jar for a kind of berry

definitions.meaning: to grate or jar on the ear or nerves
a shortened, informal name for the red soft fruit

explanation.surface: A container for some kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container for jam; it is the verb meaning to grate harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh sound grates or jars, and the word is also an informal short form of the raspberry.

clue.text: Where one lives a little in Panama, for example

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a Panama is a kind of straw hat
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: A person living in a part of Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' reads as the country, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment where an animal or plant lives.

clue.text: Content of Pandora's box is bound to need a key

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Pandora's box is locked and needs a key to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like tied up, fitting a box needing a key, but it means leap. In the myth, hope alone remained in the box after the evils escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth hope was the one thing left inside the jar when Pandora let out the world's evils.

clue.text: Waves get bigger

definitions.meaning: the long rolling movement of the sea
to grow or increase in size

explanation.surface: A forecast that the sea's waves will build.
explanation.definitionFit: The rolling heave of the sea is called a swell, and to grow larger is to swell.

clue.text: He will see what others have to say

definitions.text: He will see what others have to say

parts.words: He will see what others have to say
parts.note: someone who follows speech by watching mouths rather than listening

explanation.surface: A person promising to wait and hear people's opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See what others have to say' sounds like waiting for opinions, but here seeing is literal: speech is understood by watching mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who understands speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth, often someone deaf.
